text:
Beckett Sennecke, 20, has gone from promising rookie to top-line winger in one summer. He plays 20:24 a night, up three minutes, he is on the ice for 81% of Anaheim's power play (47% last season), and he has 22 points in 18 games, already a big piece of last season's 60. For a third overall pick that surprised a lot of people in 2024, that is a loud answer.

The chances are real. He gets to the dangerous ice; Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile of forwards for chances from the home-plate area, and Evolving-Hockey said his team created a lot more with him on. What isn't real is the finishing around him. The Ducks have scored 15.4 more goals than their chances deserve with Sennecke on the ice, the largest such gap on this list, and he is shooting 22%.

So expect the points to slow even as the role holds. Our projection lands him around 82 points. Watch his five-on-five share (45% of expected goals) as the luck evens out.
headline: Sennecke's leap, with a luck asterisk
